summary: An interior page of The Anaconda Standard for 24 June 1896, dominated by the 'Butte Department' local column at left and a dense mix of regional news, political dispatches, and commercial advertising. The left half of the page is editorial — covering Fourth of July celebration planning, Ohio Democratic convention news, a St. Patrick's commencement notice, local personals and briefs — while the right half is largely display advertising for Butte and Anaconda retailers including O. K. Lewis, The Cash Clothing Company, Brownfield-Canty Carpet Co., and Carder Bros. The political coverage leans heavily on the approaching Democratic national convention and speculation over the silver question and candidate Hartman. A June Reduction Sale on carpets anchors the centre-right of the page with large display type.
headlines: Not Many Days Left to Prepare for the Fourth of July

clipping_placements.placement_note: a brief among many local personals and notices in the Butte Department column, mid-to-lower page

juxtapositions: The Murphy infant death notice appears amid a cluster of upbeat local social items — piano recitals, athletic feats, and celebration planning — in the Butte Department column, lending it no special visual weight or mourning border.

A brief noting the infant's burial at 2 o'clock runs within a few lines of notices about a Standard Publishing company catalogue and a forthcoming athletic performance by James R. Murphy, creating an incidental Murphy-name adjacency.
